newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks close sharply lower.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks close sharply lower.

text.p: Argentine stocks took a drubbing across the board Thursday but may already have bottomed out, dealers said.

"The market continued the sharp downswing we saw yesterday on foreign selling unleashed by Wall Street's shakeout," said analyst Maximiliano Goff at Rio Research. "But despite all the turbulence, the local pension funds are still buying and I think prices are about to tilt back up."
The blue-chip MerVal index fell 2.4 percent to 724.19. It had dropped 1.4 percent Wednesday and stands 2.3 percent lower so far this week.

"The main factor behind the fall is the jump in U.S. long bond yields today and yesterday after (U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan) Greenspan warned of market euphoria and the risk of inflation. But we should bear in mind that such yield rises only hurt the markets short-term -- in 1996 even though the long bond yield edged up, the bolsa soared 25 percent and Wall Street also surged," Goff said.
"As soon as Wall Street finds its feet and bargain hunters return to the scene, we'll get a boost," another trader said.
The broad market closed off 2.6 percent, with losers thrashing winners 48 to six and 13 stocks closing flat.

Floor volume shrank to 32.5 million pesos from a very heavy tally of 48.9 million Wednesday inflated by a 15 million peso deal in Ciadea, while over-the-counter deals slowed to 97.6 million pesos from 124.5 million Wednesday.
Heaviest main-tier losers were carmaker Sevel, which fell 3.8 percent, oil concern Astra, down 3.7 percent, and oil holding company Perez Companc, off 3.1 percent.
No MerVal stocks rose and only one, construction stock Polledo, closed flat.
